Uniform pseudorandom generation with independently seeded states.

Delaunay triangulation of planar point coordinates.

Unconstrained smooth multivariate minimization requiring user first derivatives. The guarded catalog edit replaces an uninitialized workspace-length actual argument with optim%l.

The driver assembles an ordinary-kriging system from GSLIB covariance and linear-solver routines. It checks exponential covariances, closed-form weights, endpoint interpolation and independent system residuals. Broad interpolation/covariance classes only; no exhaustive spatial-statistics review. The L13 driver verifies spherical/exponential/Gaussian covariances, 21 two-observation ordinary kriging systems, closed-form weights and variances, constant-field reproduction and reflection symmetry. It separates real32 covariance error from real64 solver residuals, and does not verify the separate E2 mapping. GSLIB source-evidence hashes use UTF-8/LF normalization.

Radial one-dimensional boundary-value eigenproblem solved by finite elements. The demo checks the six n<=3 hydrogen Coulomb energies; no claim of validating the relativistic or self-consistent DFT paths. Dedicated I1b driver checks 12 nonrelativistic Coulomb energies for Z=1,2 and n<=3, including angular degeneracies, against -Z^2/(2*n^2) Hartree. First-six returned wavefunctions are checked only for finiteness. Dirac/DFT branches, wavefunction normalization and full-spectrum accuracy are not verified.

Stochastic-process modeling: deterministic stationary probabilities and AR(1) Markov discretization, not a claim of random sampling. The stationary routine uses column-stochastic matrices, while tauchen returns row-stochastic matrices; the consumer transposes explicitly. Checked driver verifies analytic two-state and rank-one equilibria, normal midpoint-cell probabilities, normalization and stationary residuals; no random sampling claim.
Matrix construction, illustrated by magic squares of orders three through six with independent row, column, diagonal and permutation checks. This mapping does not classify every other M_LA procedure.

Vector addition and component products, and column-major homogeneous translation and rotation matrices. The example checks a known point and a quarter-turn about z; broader geometry functionality is not exhaustively validated.

Signed decimal-string integer addition and subtraction beyond 64-bit range, plus unsigned interpretation of an int64 bit pattern. This is fixed-capacity decimal representation, not unlimited arbitrary precision. Dedicated A1 driver checks 3362 signed small additions/subtractions against native integer results and five exact large-decimal identities beyond int64, including carry, borrow, ordering and cancellation. Fixed capacity and overflow are not validated.

Parameter fitting remains unverified: the pinned Coulomb fit returned approximately 0.75 for noiseless observations with true coefficient 0.375 while reporting residual convergence. Source review finds fit_fcn returns model minus observed force, then passes observed force again as the least-squares target. Exact reproducer and cached GNU 16 result are retained in docs/gams-candidates/friction-double-subtraction. Ordinary algebraic force evaluation is separately checked; dynamic-state fitting remains unverified.

Constitutive friction models, with nonlinear parameter fitting and internal-state ODE integration in the reviewed source. The checked main covers algebraic Coulomb and Stribeck forces only; it does not validate parameter fitting or dynamic internal-state integration. Public LuGre state integration is now separately checked by friction-lugre-state; this does not verify the private interpolation/fitting callbacks recorded here.
Numerical evaluation of expressions parsed from text, not symbolic algebra. The demo checks double-precision multivariable Gaussian and polynomial expressions against direct Fortran formulas.

Scalar products using methods m1 through m4, each also checked with three unequal blocks against an exact answer. Single-process correctness only; no coarray or performance claim. The D1 driver checks 231 default/m1..m4 scalar products at lengths 1/7/8/17/64 against exact int64-based dyadic references, including zero products and block counts 1/3/n where valid and distinct. Contiguous inputs and single-process calls only.

Methods m1 through m4 are checked for rectangular matrix multiplication, all transpose combinations and a matrix-vector product. The demo is single-process and does not validate every implementation or coarray branch. At this pin a single explicitly false transpose flag is misrouted; the demo passes both flags whenever either is specified. Separate failing probes and the successful workaround are retained.

Fixed-width binary-string addition, subtraction, shifts and logical operations. The driver checks every eight-bit value, including carry and wraparound. This is not unlimited arbitrary-precision arithmetic. Dedicated N2 driver: 5120 exact comparisons against independent native integer references: shifts/complement/XOR over all 8-bit values, 8-bit increment/decrement, and all ordered pairs of 4-bit addition/subtraction operands. This N2 driver does not mark the separate A1 mapping verified.

Fourier/Cattaneo heat-transport code. The checked main applies its sparse BiCG solver to an independent backward-Euler discretization of the one-dimensional heat equation; it checks the discrete solution, continuous-solution error and independent matrix residuals. It does not exercise the complete evolution/Cattaneo application.

Fourier/Cattaneo heat-transport code. The checked main applies its sparse BiCG solver to an independent backward-Euler discretization of the one-dimensional heat equation; it checks the discrete solution, continuous-solution error and independent matrix residuals. It does not exercise the complete evolution/Cattaneo application.

WENO spatial reconstruction and explicit TVD Runge-Kutta integration for conservation equations. The main checks a smooth periodic advection problem against exact cell averages and verifies conservation of mass; discontinuous solutions and nonuniform grids are not covered.

WENO spatial reconstruction and explicit TVD Runge-Kutta integration for conservation equations. The main checks a smooth periodic advection problem against exact cell averages and verifies conservation of mass; discontinuous solutions and nonuniform grids are not covered. Dedicated I1 consumer checks 12 prescribed single-step-mode integrations at orders 1..3, with 8/16/32/64 dyadic steps to t=1. Independent stability-polynomial powers, exact nonautonomous forcing, exponential solutions, order-dependent grid convergence and function-evaluation counts are required. Uses documented itask=2; ordinary interval mode has a source TODO concerning final-step overshoot and is outside this verification. Spatial WENO, multistep mode, backward integration and stiffness are not verified.

Polyline simplification. The main checks one call of perpendicular-distance reduction against endpoints and an independent interpolation bound, and plots the original and reduced curves. Separate GNU 16 probes confirm incorrect radial-distance filtering and lost endpoints on consecutive perpendicular-distance calls at this pin; see the retained reproducers. The single-call example does not fix those upstream limitations.

Electrochemical models with complex-valued equivalent-circuit impedance. The main verifies resistor and capacitor impedances and their series combination against direct complex formulas at four angular frequencies. Kinetics and parameter estimation are not covered. A4 classifies the complex arithmetic interface, not an electrochemistry-specific GAMS class. Dedicated A4 consumer checks R, C and L at 216 frequency cases over 12 parameter sets, with finite complex results, status/message checks and normalized closed-form errors. Series RLC resonance and parallel RC combinations are formed by the driver, not a package circuit solver. Nonideal elements, fitting, kinetics and exceptional inputs are not verified.

Neural-network function approximation. A fixed-weight dense layer with tanh activation is compared against direct Fortran matrix multiplication and TANH. This does not test training, automatic derivatives, graph convolutions or model accuracy on a dataset. K remains broad.

Fixed-width bitset arithmetic and logical operations. The main computes an x neighbor for every cell of a two-dimensional 4-by-4 Morton grid, checking all sixteen results and wraparound against independent intrinsic integer operations.

Growable real rank-two arrays backed by spare capacity. The main checks data preservation across growth within spare capacity, reallocation, shrinking and plain-array assignment. This proof of concept is not a general-purpose container or a test of copying between container instances. Dedicated N4 driver: 16 grow/shrink traces and 128 explicit allocations. Exact active-prefix and assigned-matrix references across four fixed row counts and four overprovision factors, plus shape-changing array assignment and scope finalization. Inactive storage, zero-size and container-copy semantics unverified.

AMOS module interfaces for complex-argument Bessel functions with noninteger nonnegative order, including modified Bessel functions. The checked main compares J_0.3 and I_0.3 at 1+0.5i with independent convergent power series and K_0.5 with its closed form. Other argument regions, orders, scaling modes and Airy/Hankel routines are not validated. The upstream README warns of possible bugs. Dedicated C10 driver checks 39 complex values: J/I sequences of length two for three noninteger starting orders at three moderate right-half-plane arguments, using independent convergent power series with intrinsic Gamma, and K(1/2) using its closed form. All status/underflow flags must be zero. Scaled mode, branch-cut behavior, extreme arguments and the full library are not verified. Pinned failure: J_0.3(2-0.75i) has scaled error about 0.556 against both the independent series and an 80-digit mpmath reference. Failing source and output are retained under docs/gams-candidates/amosf90. The checked driver uses upper-right-quadrant arguments and excludes this case; no source patch or tolerance relaxation is applied.

Typed LAPACK interfaces. The checked real64 main verifies a matrix inverse residual, determinant, known eigenvalues, eigenpair residuals and orthonormality for a symmetric 3-by-3 tridiagonal matrix. Complex, single-precision and other BLAS/LAPACK wrappers are not covered. Legacy implicit external interfaces are explicitly enabled in the pinned package manifest. Dedicated D2 real64 consumer checks 132 scaled known LDU matrices and first/last-row permutations, using closed-form bidiagonal inverse factors and determinant products. Both left/right inverse residuals are accumulated with independent scalar loops. Two exact rank-deficient examples must return a false inverse status and zero determinant. Ill-conditioned/near-singular, nonsquare, complex and real32 cases are not verified.

Typed LAPACK interfaces. The checked real64 main verifies a matrix inverse residual, determinant, known eigenvalues, eigenpair residuals and orthonormality for a symmetric 3-by-3 tridiagonal matrix. Complex, single-precision and other BLAS/LAPACK wrappers are not covered. Legacy implicit external interfaces are explicitly enabled in the pinned package manifest. Dedicated D4 driver checks all 20 eigenpairs of the same Dirichlet tridiagonal matrix used by the ARPACK driver against analytic eigenvalues and sign-invariant sine eigenvectors, with residuals, orthonormality and reconstruction. This covers a real symmetric ordinary problem only; no generic solver success status is inferred from the API return. Refined from broad D4 to D4a1 for the reviewed real symmetric ordinary-eigenproblem interfaces.

Growable integer vectors. The checked main verifies growth from a two-element capacity, appended arrays, stable duplicate removal, remove/delete/pop and final compaction against independent expected contents. A checksum-guarded one-line edit fixes aliasing in unique: remove the already saved first value instead of the first array element while that array is being compacted. Empty-vector unique and all invalid-input cases are not covered. Dedicated N4 driver: 12 deterministic vector edit traces with a plain-array oracle after every operation; scalar/batch growth, fixed-value removal, positional deletion, compaction, pop-to-empty and reinitialization. Unique, sorting, invalid indices and self-aliased arguments unverified.

Character-by-character text scanning. The main reconstructs a configuration record through current/next, verifies navigation and end boundaries, and checks that peek does not move the cursor. The recovered fields are converted with ordinary internal READ and compared with known values; this is a small parser example, not a full parsing language. Dedicated N3 driver: 64 generated nonempty ASCII records checked against direct character indexing, including bidirectional traversal, immutable peeks, remaining count, end clamping and forward jump semantics. Empty input, Unicode, reverse jumps and negative moves unverified.

JSON parsing and serialization with explicit error values. The main checks numeric/string fields, missing-key reporting, compact serialization round trips and malformed-input rejection. It uses the original Erloff 2.2.0 API with a pinned compatible Strff 3.1.1 and ISO varying string 3.0.3; the Strff 4.0 dependency graph needs an unavailable GitHub mirror. No computational source is patched. Checked driver: 49 signed integer/dyadic REAL64/ASCII string objects checked before and after compact serialization against independent formulas; absent keys and two malformed inputs. Unicode, escaping, arrays and arbitrary malformed input unverified.

Typed process command-line parsing. The main launches itself once with fixed example arguments, then checks an integer, double, string, logical flag and untouched default. No supplied files or playground argument-setting changes are needed. Error exits, positional/named arguments, truncation and every syntax variant are not covered. Checked driver: 12 bounded self-invocations with short/long integer option names, signed dyadic doubles, quoted labels with spaces, absent integer defaults and present/absent logical flags. 72 exact references. Invalid options, help exits, positional/named arguments and all parser syntaxes unverified.

Key/value configuration input. The main creates and reads a tiny INI-style file with a section, comment, integer, double, logical and string, verifies known values and deletes it. A checksum-guarded manifest correction changes the invalid one-element library array into a library table; Fortran sources are unchanged. Other I/O modules and malformed-input handling are not covered. Dedicated N1 driver: Independent API consumer; pinned interfaces/implementations and available author examples reviewed without copying bodies. 36 self-contained INI files; exact signed integer, dyadic real, six true spellings, string/comment and absent-default references through wildcard section matching. Malformed inputs, false spellings, section-specific descriptors and CLI overrides unverified.

Fixed-width unsigned integer derived types. The main checks 16/32-bit upper boundaries, 32-bit arithmetic above the signed boundary, comparisons, modular addition/subtraction and conversion of a negative assignment. It imports the current int_m conversion API explicitly. This is not arbitrary-precision arithmetic or validation of every kind, operation or C interoperability path.

Functional unit-testing framework. The main runs three specification-style cases checking a small user-written Simpson formula against known constant, linear and quadratic integrals. The numerical formula belongs to the example, not the package. Parallel testing, generators and the complete framework are not validated. Checked driver: 289 exact integer equality outcomes, 17 combined assertion/failure counts, plus two passing test-runner cases checking 64 integer sums and an exact binary real. The arithmetic examples are user calculations, not numerical algorithms supplied by Veggies. Intentionally failed result objects are inspected without running a failing suite. Filtering, generators, full diagnostics and parallelism unverified.

Token-based expression parsing with user-supplied callbacks. The main checks precedence, parentheses, right-associative exponentiation, square root and unary minus against five exact results. A checksum-guarded edit moves a host-independent library callback to module scope after the original layout crashed in the sandbox; parsing rules are unchanged. The author documents global registrations, fixed precedences and missing syntax validation; concurrent parsers and malformed expressions are not supported by this example. Dedicated N3 driver: Independent integer callback consumer; 437 bounded binary expressions checked against direct arithmetic, including precedence, nested parentheses, exact division, right-associative powers and ignored spaces. Unary registration excluded: retained probe returns 1 instead of -1 for 1-1-1 when unary minus also marks the minus token right-associative. No parser patch; malformed syntax, real functions, overflow and registration isolation unverified.

SQLite wrapper with bundled SQLite 3.30.1 C sources. The checked main opens an in-memory database, creates a table, inserts three values, verifies count and average, reaches SQLITE_DONE and closes resources. It does not cover persistent files, concurrent use, transactions or the complete SQLite API. Explicit GitLab-to-GitHub alias pins ISO varying string; no source edits. Dedicated N1 driver: Independent API consumer; pinned interfaces/implementations and available author examples reviewed without copying bodies. In-memory SQL consumer: 64 prepared/bound integer/dyadic-real inserts with reset; commit plus rolled-back update/insertion; five exact aggregates and 43 ordered row references after deletion. Disk persistence, concurrency, text/NULL and error recovery unverified.

Structured error lists and logging. The checked main collects two fatal validation messages, filters one by OUT_OF_BOUNDS, checks counts and diagnostic text, and prints both messages. The pinned compatible Strff 3.1.1 avoids the unavailable exceptional_numbers mirror requested through Strff 4.0. No library source edits. This does not cover all logging levels, filtering operators or concurrent use. Checked driver: 48 append steps with exact diagnostic membership and parity category counts. Previous copied snapshots retain their size and exclude each newly added message. Other filters, severity classes and memory behavior unverified.

Customizable text tokenization. The checked main uses a module callback to split comma, space and tab-separated fields, verifies all three tokens and checks clearing the list. This is lexical splitting, not expression evaluation. No source edits. Malformed input, every callback combination and token object storage are not covered. Dedicated N3 driver: 64 field streams and empty input with constructed exact expected fields. Five separator bytes, repeated/leading/trailing separators, ignored fields and both stored and optional validator/ignore callbacks. Default validator, quoting/escaping and Unicode rules unverified.

Simple fixed-width integer sets. The checked main verifies duplicate rejection, removal and sorted contents for 32-bit values, and duplicate rejection for a 64-bit value above the 32-bit range. Membership is checked from public data, not a separate membership API. No source edits. Performance, every boundary and all operations are not validated. Dedicated N4 driver: Eight paired INT32/INT64 edit traces checked against a Boolean membership oracle after every edit, with duplicate and absent removals, clear/reuse, 32-bit sorting and large 64-bit values. 64-bit sorting, integer extrema and reuse after destroy unverified.

Reference-counted resource management. Adapted from the author example: a user type extends sp_smart_pointer_t and implements free. The checked main shares one integer resource, verifies reference counts and shared target, checks no premature cleanup and confirms exactly one cleanup after subroutine return. No source edits. This is not exhaustive compiler finalization conformance testing. Checked driver: 64 owned integer-array resources with nested aliases. Counts 1/2/3/2/1, target association, shared mutation, no premature cleanup and exactly-once cleanup/checksum on subroutine exit. Reassignment, cycles, explicit release, arrays of pointers, leaks and other compiler finalization behavior unverified.

Numerical routines from the RPN calculator, called directly without its interactive interface. The checked main verifies a negative cube root, sinc and sech at zero, beta(2,3), modified Bessel I0 at zero, and integer gcd/lcm against known results. A checksum-guarded manifest correction sets source-form=default so .f and .f90 files use their respective forms. No numerical sources are changed. The tests do not establish accuracy over full argument ranges or validate the complete calculator. Dedicated C4 consumer verifies real sinc against a 64-term independent series and sech against a stable exponential formula for 133 real arguments, including zero and signed near-zero values. Finite values, symmetry, range and scalar/array agreement are checked. This driver does not verify the separate C2 cube-root mapping or complex overloads.

Numerical routines from the RPN calculator, called directly without its interactive interface. The checked main verifies a negative cube root, sinc and sech at zero, beta(2,3), modified Bessel I0 at zero, and integer gcd/lcm against known results. A checksum-guarded manifest correction sets source-form=default so .f and .f90 files use their respective forms. No numerical sources are changed. The tests do not establish accuracy over full argument ranges or validate the complete calculator. Dedicated C7 consumer verifies 128 positive integer/half-integer beta pairs with independent factorial identities, plus symmetry and both one-step recurrences (512 evaluations). Finite positive values and relative error within 2e-13 are required. C10 Bessel functions, complex beta, poles, large arguments and overflow handling are outside this driver.

Numerical routines from the RPN calculator, called directly without its interactive interface. The checked main verifies a negative cube root, sinc and sech at zero, beta(2,3), modified Bessel I0 at zero, and integer gcd/lcm against known results. A checksum-guarded manifest correction sets source-form=default so .f and .f90 files use their respective forms. No numerical sources are changed. The tests do not establish accuracy over full argument ranges or validate the complete calculator. Dedicated GAMS B driver: GCD and LCM checked over nonnegative operands 0..64 against independent divisor/multiple searches. LCM(0,0) divides by zero at this pin and is excluded; signed conventions and overflow are not verified.

NetCDF4 array and attribute I/O. The checked main writes a 2-by-3 double-precision array with dimension names and a kelvin units attribute, closes the file, reopens and verifies every value and the attribute, then deletes the sandbox file. Native NetCDF and HDF5 development packages and include/library paths are pinned in the build recipe. No source edits. It does not cover every type/rank, compression, slicing or malformed files. Checked driver: 24 REAL64 matrix NetCDF4 files written by the wrapper. Native NetCDF C API checks named dimension lengths, reversed C axis order and all 210 indexed values using zero-based C indices; wrapper full reads check the same 210 formula values and units. Both APIs share the underlying NetCDF library; compression, other kinds/ranks and external implementations unverified.

CODATA physical constants. The checked main imports the explicit 2022 edition, computes the energy of a 500 nm photon in joules and electron volts, and compares it with independent decimal reference values. The source modules are pre-generated; no network request or Python generation is needed to use them. No source edits. This is a check of three constants and one calculation, not revalidation of the complete CODATA tables or uncertainty propagation. Dedicated R driver: Independent API consumer; pinned interfaces/implementations and available author examples reviewed without copying bodies. Three SI-defining constants and 24 photon-energy references from independent exact Python Fraction arithmetic, with joule/electron-volt conversions. NIST 2022 CODATA source reviewed. Other constants and uncertain values unverified.

Derived types and constructors for multidimensional array bounds. The checked main reconstructs and round-trips bounds [-1:1,4:5], traverses exactly six elements using stored bounds and verifies their sum of 270. No source edits. It does not cover all dimensions, vector/tensor wrappers, empty arrays or invalid bounds. This is an indexing utility, not a numerical solver. Dedicated R driver: Independent API consumer; pinned interfaces/implementations and available author examples reviewed without copying bodies. 784 nonempty rank-2 arrays with negative/zero/positive origins and asymmetric extents. Exact bound literals and independent arithmetic-progression traversal sums. Empty extents and aggregate constructors unverified.

Gauss-Kronrod quadrature-rule generation. A checksum-guarded adapter exposes the original internal procedures as module playground_kronrod, removes the large driver loop and declares app as the library directory; The consumer uses the wrapped module instead of running the original batch drivers. Procedure bodies, constants and precision settings are unchanged. The main generates the symmetric 7-point rule, checks six even polynomial integrals through degree 10 at 40-decimal-place tolerance with MPFUN arithmetic, and prints double-precision summaries. Only the unchanged MPFUN dependency is shared. This is a rule generator, not an adaptive integrator or full validation of every rule/order.

Pure Fortran regular expressions by Edward Higgins, distinct from perazz/fortran-regex already selected under fortran-regex. The main checks matching and nonmatching anchored decimal measurements, matched substring, comma/space splitting and replacement. No source edits or native regex library. Pattern whitespace is ignored unless escaped; the author documents missing capture references and other features, so PCRE compatibility and all patterns are not claimed. Checked driver: Exhaustive 340 strings of lengths 1..4 over 01a., each checked against decimal and identifier patterns using an independent character-state grammar: 680 comparisons. Empty strings, malformed patterns, captures, splitting/replacement and full regex compatibility unverified.

Programmatic Fortran edit descriptors. The main generates and applies integer, character and fixed-decimal real formats, checks exact aligned output, and verifies a zero-padded integer. The registry stdlib dependency is mapped to a pinned Git source and manifest version; compatible stdlib objects are reused. No Fortran source edits. Arrays, complex values, user-defined I/O and every descriptor/control mode are not covered. Dedicated N1 driver: Independent API consumer; pinned interfaces/implementations and available author examples reviewed without copying bodies. Generated integer and fixed-point edit descriptors compared with independently constructed native Fortran format strings, including overflow fields, minimum digits and concatenated columns. Other descriptor families, locale and cross-compiler rounding unverified. Reference accounts for reviewed FED normalization: zero minimum digits omit .m, and real widths increase to at least d+2. Retained native-format assumptions were consumer reference errors, not upstream defects.

Type-erased intrinsic values returned through any_type. The checked main returns an integer, a double-precision real and a character value through one function, retrieves each using its matching type, and checks exact values. No source edits. The author documents undefined results for mismatched type/rank conversions; the example does not validate all ranks, kinds, custom extensions or invalid conversions. Dedicated N4 driver: Independent API consumer of fresh nonempty typed buffers; 32 groups and 1712 exact scalar/array references. Original arrays are mutated after wrapping to check owned copies. Empty-string and empty-array runtime failures are retained, not fixed. Initial assignment-import compile failure was a consumer API error. Reassignment, mismatched types and all ranks/kinds unverified.

FIFO container using C allocations and byte copies. The main enqueues four 64-bit C-interoperable integers, verifies count and exact retrieval order, frees every popped allocation with C free, checks empty-pop behavior and destroys the queue. No source edits. The implementation uses GNU LOC and raw byte storage; the example makes no portability claim for arbitrary derived types, pointer-owning values, threading or every compiler. The class-specific N4 driver checks 160 copied two-int64 records against an independent FIFO model, interleaved pushes/pops, three drain/refill cycles, empty-pop null pointers, independent queues and freeing all popped allocations. No pointer-owning or misaligned payload is certified.

UTF-8 string handling using one array element per encoded Unicode code point. The main verifies a round trip, code point count, substring, search and replacement of accented text, and prints the results. No source edits. Combining marks remain separate code points; grapheme segmentation, normalization and malformed-input handling are not validated. Dedicated N3 driver: 33 valid UTF-8 fixtures encoded independently from integer code points. Exact round trips, positive substrings, single-code-point search, expanding replacement and deletion across one-to-four-byte sequences including combining marks. Malformed encoding, normalization, grapheme and multi-code-point search semantics unverified.

Serial system_clock and CPU timers. The checked main computes the exact sum of integers 1 through 100000, checks finite nonnegative elapsed times and prints the sum and timings. The root manifest VERSION placeholder is replaced with adapter version 0.0.0; the pinned source commit identifies the actual library. FACE is pinned to an already used revision. No Fortran source edits. MPI/OpenMP timers are not enabled or tested; sandbox timings vary and are not benchmark guarantees. Checked driver: 16 reused wall/CPU timer pairs, nloops averaging and exact integer work checksums. Reported durations multiplied by nloops must fall between native inner/outer SYSTEM_CLOCK or CPU_TIME brackets, allowing four wall ticks or 2 microseconds CPU resolution slack. No latency or speed benchmark claim. Pause/resume, wrapping, invalid calls, MPI/OpenMP timers and other platforms unverified.

Assertions for integer scalars and arrays plus approximate real comparison with an explicit tolerance. The main captures an intentional failed comparison as a logical status and message, checks both, and continues successfully. No source edits; matches the existing Any dependency revision. Not a validation of every type, rank, tolerance convention, custom comparator or test-framework integration. The S3 driver checks three positive assertions and 13 captured scalar/vector comparisons, including failures, both exact tolerance boundaries and independently checked logical outcomes and diagnostic labels/status prefixes. The separate R2 mapping remains source-supported.

Error status and message handling. A custom reciprocal routine uses catch_error and set_success. The main checks a successful result, zero rejection with an exact code and message, and a subsequent successful call clearing the error. No source edits. The reciprocal is only a driver, not a mathematical procedure supplied by errstat. Optional omitted-status termination and user-defined task/message repositories are not exercised. The R3 driver checks nine success/failure/recovery calls with exact codes/messages, signed-zero and NaN input rejection, independent copied statuses, appended context and explicit reset. The illustrative safe square-root ratio is supplied by the driver, not errstat.

Generic singly linked list for small datasets. The main checks integer and real payloads in insertion order, list size, iteration count, emptying, retained capacity and the value stored after reuse; iterator and list cleanup are explicit. A checksum-guarded compatibility edit removes PURE from node_init, whose result has a polymorphic allocatable component. Constructor allocation and copying are unchanged, and the call sites are impure. This patched root retains its own small archive instead of sharing an unmodified graph export. No display dependency is needed for the custom consumer. Large-data performance, all mutation operations and ownership of pointer-containing derived types are not validated. Dedicated N4 driver: 20 heterogeneous linked-list cycles checking exact typed values and insertion order, replacing dynamic types in retained nodes, retained capacity, iterator exhaustion, empty/reuse and explicit finalization. Empty-list iterator creation and mutation during iteration unverified.

String enclosure with automatically matched closing brackets and explicit delimiters. The main checks nested bracket reversal, square brackets, quotation marks, custom opening/closing strings and disabled autoclosing, and prints examples. No source edits; matches the existing FED dependency revision. This is formatting, not parsing or escaping untrusted text. Dedicated N3 driver: Exhaustive strings through width three from nine paired/ordinary symbols with three payloads, checked against an independent SELECT CASE bracket involution. Automatic reverse closures, literal repetition, explicit closures and empty cases; Unicode delimiter semantics unverified.

Xoroshiro128+ pseudo-random generator. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged m_random.f90 and uses -fwrapv for its intentional signed-integer wraparound. Two fresh generators replay 10000 seeded uniform draws exactly; the main checks the implementation range [0,1), broad uniform/normal/Poisson(4) moment tolerances, nonnegative counts and unit circle/sphere norms. These are deterministic smoke checks, not statistical quality or cryptographic validation. OpenMP, jump independence, large Poisson rates and all distributions are not covered. A separate hosted reproducer confirms that set_seed does not clear the cached second normal after an odd normal() call; use a fresh generator to restart normal sequences. The selected replay uses fresh objects. Dedicated L6a21 driver checks 15 interleaved streams against unsigned-Python prefixes and rolling hashes, exact 52-bit integer/uniform conversion, seeded restarts and zero/default/two explicit jumps. Jump references use independent GF(2) transition-matrix exponentiation to 2**64. This establishes fixed bitstream and seed/jump API behavior, not statistical quality or thread independence; the cached-normal reseeding defect remains unresolved.

Xoroshiro128+ pseudo-random generator. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged m_random.f90 and uses -fwrapv for its intentional signed-integer wraparound. Two fresh generators replay 10000 seeded uniform draws exactly; the main checks the implementation range [0,1), broad uniform/normal/Poisson(4) moment tolerances, nonnegative counts and unit circle/sphere norms. These are deterministic smoke checks, not statistical quality or cryptographic validation. OpenMP, jump independence, large Poisson rates and all distributions are not covered. A separate hosted reproducer confirms that set_seed does not clear the cached second normal after an odd normal() call; use a fresh generator to restart normal sequences. The selected replay uses fresh objects. Dedicated L6 consumer checks exact replay with fresh seeded objects, 60000 normal and 60000 small-rate Poisson samples against broad analytic moment/zero-probability tolerances, and 3000 circle plus 3000 sphere samples against exact norm references and broad coordinate moments. These are fixed-seed deterministic smoke checks, not statistical or cryptographic quality certification. Fresh allocations avoid the known cached-normal reseeding issue; that issue remains unresolved. Poisson rates >=10/rejection sampling, parallel/jump independence and full distribution coverage are not verified.

Numeric text parsing. FPM 0.12 rejects the upstream features/profiles tables; a checksum-guarded manifest adaptation removes them and supplies the intended -fno-range-check compiler setting explicitly. The Fortran sources are unchanged and development-only benchmark dependencies are not built. The main checks decimal/scientific and Fortran D-exponent parsing, the largest positive signed int64, hexadecimal parsing, invalid-input status and exponent-overflow status. Correct rounding for every input, all formats, underflow, platforms and speed claims are not validated. The class-specific N3 driver checks 154 calls, including 129 exact dyadic decimals, signed integer boundaries, binary/hex input, Fortran D exponent, one binary64 halfway rounding case and six invalid/overflow outcomes. It does not certify correct rounding for all inputs or complete-token consumption.

Documented configuration values. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged m_config.f90. The main creates its own tiny configuration file, overrides integer, logical, string and grouped real defaults, reads a dynamically sized real array, checks every value and clears the configuration. No uploaded data file or external service is required. Command-line parsing, invalid-file diagnostics and all string/array/grouping behavior are not validated. Dedicated N1 driver: Independent API consumer; pinned interfaces/implementations and available author examples reviewed without copying bodies. 24 fresh configuration objects/files with exact typed scalars, nested keys, dynamic arrays and retained defaults. Valid generated inputs only; malformed files, unknown keys, repeated reads and CLI inputs unverified.

Nearest-neighbor and radius searches. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged src-f90/kdtree2.f90; the archived upstream single-precision setting is retained. The checked main builds a tree for 30 deterministic 2D points, compares four nearest indices and squared distances against an independent direct search, and checks radius-search count, membership, distances and uniqueness. The original Academic Free License 1.1 is retained. No source edits. The implementation has global search state and is not offered as thread-safe; the old interface, C++ code, every dimension and large-scale performance are not validated. The class-specific N5 driver additionally verifies 36 3D searches over 48 points against exhaustive real64 distances: k=1,5,48, radii squared 0/0.125/4 and both storage rearrangement modes. Tie ordering is not prescribed; complete radius sets and uniqueness are checked. This driver does not separately verify the broad P mapping.

procedure_mappings.notes: Portable numerical kinds, formats and number/string conversions. The latest archive is blocked by a symlink, so this entry uses exactly the older revision already verified as a BeFoR64 dependency. The checked main calls penf_init, verifies integer and real conversion round trips with status checks, zero-padded integer output, real byte size and formatted real output. Sources are unchanged; this adds an independent editable main for the pinned library. Every kind, character encoding, endian platform and invalid conversion is not validated. The R1 driver verifies ISO kind correspondence, six type widths, public size/max/normal-minimum constants, byte inquiries, byte order, repeated initialization and measured real32/real64 roundoff. It does not verify the separate N3 conversion mapping, quadruple precision or arbitrary platforms.

Forward-mode automatic differentiation with dual numbers. The main checks the upstream scalar example against its analytical value and derivative, a two-variable polynomial gradient and a square 2-by-2 Jacobian against exact formulas. GNU heap trampolines support the internal callback procedures in the restricted sandbox. Library sources are unchanged. The author limits jacobian to square problems and documents incomplete intrinsic coverage; sparse interfaces, every overload and all failure modes are not validated.

Scientific utilities. The main sorts repeated and negative integers, builds a k-d tree for 20 deterministic 2D points and compares the nearest point with an independent direct search. The OpenMP metapackage is resolved explicitly and -fopenmp is enabled; the execution sandbox still uses one thread. No source edits. The broad library is compiled, but this driver does not validate all containers, random generators, mathematical utilities or parallel performance. The checked GAMS driver uses explicit stable=true only. A mixed-setting probe fails with stable=false on 16 equal integer32 values; source/hash/result are retained in docs/gams-candidates/coretran-sort.

Scientific utilities. The main sorts repeated and negative integers, builds a k-d tree for 20 deterministic 2D points and compares the nearest point with an independent direct search. The OpenMP metapackage is resolved explicitly and -fopenmp is enabled; the execution sandbox still uses one thread. No source edits. The broad library is compiled, but this driver does not validate all containers, random generators, mathematical utilities or parallel performance. A broader nearest-neighbor probe fails on a valid 31-point query; its source, hash and result are retained in docs/gams-candidates/coretran-nearest. This procedure has no checked GAMS driver.

Version 1 multivariate interpolation using sparse Delaunay simplices. Version 2 bundles BQPD with a research-only redistribution notice, so the selected pin uses the earlier MIT-licensed version 1 with its bundled SLATEC/BLAS/LAPACK sources. An FPM wrapper retains fixed/free source forms, legacy implicit typing/interfaces and -fallow-argument-mismatch for the SLATEC scalar-zero/zero-stride BLAS convention. OpenMP is enabled to link the library; the checked driver uses the serial routine. It verifies exact linear-function reproduction at three interior 2D points, zero status codes, valid simplex indices and barycentric weight sums/signs. No numerical source edits. Convex-hull projection/extrapolation, all degenerate inputs, high-dimensional behavior and parallel variants are not validated. The class-specific E2 driver verifies six 3D interior queries with ten irregular points, three output fields, affine/constant reproduction, unique nondegenerate simplex vertices and barycentric reconstruction of preserved original coordinates. The nonlinear field is checked as piecewise-linear interpolation; exact nonlinear-function recovery and the empty-circumsphere property are not certified.

NumPy NPY writing. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged src/npy.f90. The main writes a 2-by-3 real64 matrix, checks version-2 magic, dtype/order header, exact binary payload and file size, and prints the matrix and header. A separate hosted probe captures the actual file bytes and NumPy independently loads the expected shape, dtype and exact values with pickle disabled. No source edits. The author no longer actively maintains the project. Other kinds/ranks, big-endian platforms and NPZ archive operations are not validated; the browser displays the checked summary rather than offering a general NPY-file download. Checked driver: 35 REAL64 matrix NPY files independently read using native stream I/O: magic/version, little-endian dtype, Fortran order, exact shape, byte size and 420 payload values. Scope is little-endian GNU/Linux; empty arrays, other kinds, NPZ and external NumPy loading unverified.

procedure_mappings.notes: Selected Fortran Template Library instantiations: integer dynamic arrays and ftlString-to-integer hash maps, plus their unmodified support modules. A checksum-guarded adapter adds CPP-disabled module/dependency declarations so FPM 0.12 can discover modules emitted by templates. Original and adapted compiler-preprocessed output match apart from blank lines. Implicit-external checking is left at the upstream convention to avoid a GNU diagnostic in a character-length specification expression. The checked main verifies array growth, contents and pop, map insertion/replacement, presence, lookup and erase, then explicitly deletes both containers. Sources otherwise remain unchanged, and template headers remain in the source archive. Other instantiations, general algorithms, regex and every ownership/finalization case are not offered or validated. Checked driver: Eight 128-step traces compare all dynamic-array values and 17 map membership/value slots against plain-array oracles. Growth, LIFO pops, replacement, conditional deletion, final drain and explicit destruction. Iterators, object copies, missing-key Get, clear/reuse and thread safety unverified.

Serial QNSTOP for bound-constrained stochastic and global optimization. An FPM wrapper selects unmodified REAL_PRECISION, ZIGARRAY, QNSTOPS and bundled BLAS/LAPACK sources. Explicit CPP suffix handling lets FPM discover .f95 files. Legacy implicit typing/interfaces and argument-mismatch compatibility retain the upstream calling conventions. The seeded two-variable quadratic example checks normal stopping status, bounds, objective value and distance from its known minimizer. It is an accuracy smoke test, not a general global-optimum guarantee. The parallel QNSTOPP driver, noisy objectives, all stopping rules and performance are not validated. Dedicated G2 consumer checks four seeded diagonal-quadratic box problems with known interior minimizers in two/three variables. Verifies normal stopping status, feasibility, finite output, evaluation count, returned-objective consistency and unchanged coordinate/objective tolerances. Active-bound probes failed the position tolerance at both 500 and 2000 iterations; source and actual results are retained under docs/gams-candidates/qnstop. Those face probes and an unreached corner fixture are not counted as verified. Seeds use the pinned GNU intrinsic RNG; this is a deterministic accuracy smoke check, not a general global guarantee. Noisy objectives, parallel variants and all stopping/input modes are not verified.

Serial FFTW Poisson solvers. An FPM wrapper selects the Fortran library modules, retains upstream template includes, adds CPP-disabled USE declarations for the FPM dependency scanner, declares unused MPI/PFFT modules external for scanning, enables CPP and links Debian FFTW 3.3.10 single/double and thread libraries. MPI/PFFT and C/C++ bindings are not offered. The checked double-precision periodic 1D spectral problem compares its solution with sin(2*pi*x) at 32 points. Other boundary conditions, finite-difference modes, nonuniform grids, higher-dimensional solvers, single precision and parallel execution are not validated. A class-specific I2 driver additionally verifies spectral and second-order finite-difference periodic solvers at 16/32/64 points against exact two-mode discrete solutions, finite-difference residuals, zero-mean gauge and reuse of each plan for zero forcing (12 solves). Finite-difference errors are separated from solver error; other boundary conditions, dimensions and parallel variants remain unverified.

LMDB key-value database bindings with Debian LMDB 0.9.31. A checksum-guarded compatibility edit selects the existing signed-kind fallback rather than GNU unsigned extension kinds, which are unavailable without enabling nondefault unsigned support. The checked consumer creates a small sandbox-local database, inserts and updates a value, verifies committed reads and rollback after an aborted update, deletes the key and checks MDB_NOTFOUND, then closes and removes both database files. No persistent storage is provided. Large mappings, concurrent writers/readers, all cursor interfaces and other platforms are not validated. Checked driver: 64 fixed-width text keys/values: committed inserts, aborted replacement of every value, then committed updates and deletion of keys divisible by three. Reverse-order reads compare all 192 key states with independent integer formulas and MDB_NOTFOUND. Concurrent transactions, persistence across processes, cursors, duplicate keys and large maps unverified.

Fortran bindings to Lua 5.4, linked with Debian Lua 5.4.7. The manifest library name lua-5.4 is adapted to Linux lua5.4; library sources are unchanged. Adapted from the upstream in-memory string example, the consumer defines a Lua function, passes an integer from Fortran, checks Lua load/call status and function type, verifies the returned integer and closes the state. External scripts, callbacks from Lua to Fortran, arbitrary Lua modules and all bindings are not validated. Dedicated S consumer checks exact factorial, sums-of-squares and signed-polynomial results plus real Pythagorean norms across the Fortran/Lua boundary. Checks return types, stack balance, expected runtime/syntax diagnostics and reuse of the same state after errors (128 integer and five real successes). Independent Lua scripts and Fortran references; no external script files. Arbitrary modules, callbacks to Fortran, userdata, concurrency and full language/binding coverage are not verified.

POSIX/SysV bindings on the playground 64-bit Linux/glibc environment. The source library is unchanged. The manifest features/profiles tables are removed for FPM 0.12 compatibility and their Linux preprocessor flag is supplied explicitly. A 13-byte sandbox-local file is created, its size is checked through c_stat, then c_unlink removes it and Fortran INQUIRE confirms removal. Other operating systems, process creation, networking, IPC, signals, threads and all ABI structures are not validated or promised in the restricted sandbox. Checked driver: 129 Linux POSIX file lifecycles with generated binary bytes: c_stat sizes versus expected lengths and INQUIRE, byte content, c_unlink disappearance and failed stat afterward. Permissions, symlinks, errno, directories and non-Linux platforms unverified.

Serial derivative-free, bound-constrained multiobjective optimization. An FPM wrapper selects the unchanged solver, surrogate and test-function sources with bundled SLATEC support and links system LP64 BLAS/LAPACK rather than recompiling those bundled libraries. OpenMP linking is enabled, but the checked run uses the serial driver and one execution thread; heap trampolines support internal callbacks in the sandbox. Adapted from the author serial driver and CONVEX function, the seeded 3-variable/2-objective example uses a small evaluation budget, checks feasible design bounds, recomputes both quadratic objectives independently and verifies that no returned point dominates another. It requires multiple distinct trade-off points. This checks the finite returned set, not convergence to the exact global Pareto front or comparative performance. Parallel evaluation, checkpoint recovery, every surrogate and other problem classes are not validated. Dedicated G2 driver checks two squared-distance objectives against an exact Pareto segment in two/three dimensions, with two intrinsic-seed settings per dimension. Every archive point has independently recomputed objectives and projection identities; each run has at least five points within relative distance 0.05 and their segment span exceeds 0.25. The full archive is not uniformly near the Pareto set: the failed all-point 0.15-distance assertion is retained in docs/gams-candidates/vtmop-archive-distance. Both seed settings produced the same observed archive per dimension; they are not evidence of independent stochastic search.

procedure_mappings.derivatives: User-supplied analytical state Jacobian in this demo; tangent initial conditions select the rate sensitivity.
procedure_mappings.notes: Selected FATODE explicit Runge-Kutta tangent-linear integrator, linked to native BLAS/LAPACK. The FPM wrapper compiles unchanged TLM/ERK_TLM/ERK_TLM_f90_Integrator.F90; bundled precompiled platform binaries are not used. The example augments exponential decay with a constant rate state and differentiates the initial rate using the tangent-linear model, checking the state, rate, and both sensitivities against analytical formulas. It explicitly selects the supplied analytical Jacobian and enables tangent-variable adaptive error control; the initial default finite-difference Jacobian settings missed the requested sensitivity accuracy. No numerical library edits. Implicit/stiff solvers, adjoint integration, sparse solver variants and all ERK methods are not offered or verified.

Dedicated D8 driver checks continuous/discrete Lyapunov with transpose options and Schur reuse using constructed known solutions, finite outputs, explicit success status and independently recomputed residuals. See docs/gams-matrix-equations.md for equations, storage, scaling and limitations.

Serial classic Fortran ARPACK-NG interfaces, built from unchanged SRC .f files, the documented UTIL support set, and upstream debug/statistics initializers. The wrapper uses native LP64 BLAS/LAPACK and excludes PARPACK/MPI and generated C bindings. The upstream second_NONE timing stub disables ARPACK internal elapsed-time statistics; playground build/run timings still work. Adapted from the author symmetric reverse-communication example, the main computes three smallest eigenpairs of a 20-by-20 symmetric tridiagonal operator, checks convergence status/count, analytical eigenvalues and eigenvector residual norms. A deterministic nonzero initial residual avoids dependence on random initialization. Nonsymmetric/complex modes, shift-invert, generalized problems and parallel execution are not validated. Dedicated D4 driver checks the three smallest and three largest eigenpairs of the 20-by-20 Dirichlet tridiagonal (2 diagonal,-1 off-diagonal), with explicit starting residual, convergence/extraction status, analytical eigenvalues and sign-invariant sine eigenvector comparisons, equation residuals and orthonormality. Generalized, nonsymmetric, shift-invert and arbitrary spectra are not verified. Refined from broad D4 to D4a1 for the reviewed real symmetric ordinary-eigenproblem interfaces.

Structured error handling and validation. The upstream FPM library sources are unchanged; unlimited free-form line length accommodates existing long source lines. Adapted from the author example, the main checks a valid bounded integer in a Result object, rejects an out-of-range integer with expected code 105, checks two retained application trace entries, and triggers a custom noncritical warning while execution continues. The example uses fixed values rather than interactive input. All Result ranks/types, critical-error termination, all validation criteria and every trace-propagation path are not validated. Dedicated R2 consumer checks 102 integer/real32/real64 inclusive bound comparisons against native logical expressions, including one-sided/equal bounds and nearest representable values inside/outside both endpoints. All 30 expected rejections must retain code 105, a supplied custom message and one supplied trace entry. No error is triggered. Other criteria, reversed/missing bounds, NaNs, critical termination and the separate R3 handling mapping are not verified.

Runtime assertion checks in pure procedures, built with ASSERTIONS=1 so enforcement is enabled in the cached library. A checksum-guarded manifest edit adds the upstream include directory; library sources and headers are unchanged. The main checks preconditions and postconditions around a pure square-root function. A separate sandbox probe compiles successfully, intentionally calls assert(.false.), and verifies nonzero termination with the expected descriptive diagnostic and unchanged library artifacts, demonstrating that checks were not compiled away. Multi-image/coarray callbacks and every macro variant are not validated. Full current upstream license terms, including its enhancement-contribution provision, are retained under LicenseRef-Berkeley-Assert rather than labeling them as an unmodified standard BSD license. Checked driver: 65 bounded square evaluations inside pure pre/postcondition assertions, plus one deliberately false assertion in a self-invoked child. Parent requires nonzero exit and the specified diagnostic, proving enforcement in the existing enabled library. Child failure is expected and checked. Other macros, callbacks, multi-image behavior and disabled builds unverified. Upstream custom license terms remain unchanged.

Native Fortran FMM2D source set selected from the upstream makefile with optional C++ fast kernels disabled. OpenMP and portable -O2 are enabled; the visitor sandbox uses one execution thread and retains bounds checks. Checksum-guarded compatibility edits skip zero-point multipole/local evaluations and zero-source neighbor calls before passing one-past-end array elements. The inverse reorder helper declares its arrays with the actual n extent rather than the legacy dummy extent 1. Source and target branches receive matching guards; formulas are unchanged. The checked real Laplace driver evaluates 512 deterministic sources at 16 separate targets and compares with an independent charge-weighted log-distance sum. A separate source-and-target probe also checks all source potentials by direct summation with self-interactions excluded, exercising the source-side guards. The code is classified as a structured kernel-matrix application and Green-function evaluation related to PDEs, not as a complete boundary-value solver. Helmholtz, biharmonic/Stokes, dipoles, gradients/Hessians, every complex/vector interface and parallel speedups are not validated. The small accuracy check is not a performance benchmark.

Selected unmodified modules types, utils, lapack, mesh, splines and sorting, wrapped for FPM and linked to compatible LP64 BLAS/LAPACK. HDF5, AMOS/special functions, optimization and other unselected modules are not included. The main reproduces a cubic polynomial with the consistent-boundary cubic spline and checks its value, first derivative and second derivative on a denser grid against exact formulas. It checks exponential-mesh endpoints, monotonicity and the requested last/first spacing ratio, then sorts repeated/negative integers against an exact answer. General nonpolynomial interpolation error, extrapolation, every boundary condition, other sorting interfaces and all utility routines are not validated. Dedicated E1 consumer checks exact degree-0..3 polynomial reproduction on three uniform grids and a nonuniform grid, including first/second derivatives at 65 queries. Optional outputs and reversed query order are compared independently. Uses the API default consistent-cubic endpoint conditions; extrapolation, nonpolynomial convergence, other boundary choices and the separate N6 sorting mapping are not verified.

Mimetic vector-calculus library with pinned Julienne and Assert dependencies. A single-image coarray build is used. The checked consumer adapts the author's extended Gauss-divergence example to f=x**2/2 and v=x on a 64-cell unit interval. It checks the two volume integrals against 1/3 and 1/6, the boundary flux against 1/2, finiteness and the conservation residual using single-precision tolerances. The command-line parsing and shell display calls of the upstream example are omitted. Library numerical sources are unchanged. Other 2D/3D operators, time integration and convergence orders are not validated. Original Berkeley Lab license terms, including the enhancements clause, are retained; this is not labeled plain BSD-3-Clause.

Unmodified Fortran library sources selected from the upstream native makefile and wrapped for FPM. The checked example adapts the upstream hydrogen test to Z=1 and computes all six (n,l) states through n=3 on an exponential radial mesh. It requires solver convergence, finite energies and agreement with the analytical nonrelativistic energies -1/(2*n**2) within 1e-7 Hartree. Relativistic Dirac, Poisson and self-consistent density-functional calculations are present in the library but not exercised by this example. C/Python bindings and optional extra integration/interpolation/LAPACK sources are outside the selected native source set.

Unmodified mixed C/Fortran POSIX system library in the Linux/glibc sandbox. The checked example creates a local directory with owner-only permissions, writes and reads back the integer 42, checks directory and regular-file types, removes both and confirms cleanup. Other system calls, processes, networking, permissions changes and Windows portability are not validated or promised. Upstream development dependencies and applications are not part of the consumer demonstration. Checked driver: 65 Linux sandbox file create/read/remove traces under an owner-only directory. Generated binary contents and native directory/regular-file predicates are checked; files and directory must disappear after removal. Other system calls, permissions inspection, symlinks and Windows behavior unverified.

Fortran/C bindings linked to pinned Debian Tcl/Tk 8.6 development libraries. A checksum-guarded include edit selects Debian's tcl8.6/tcl.h path for the C macro wrappers; interfaces and calculation code are unchanged. Adapted from the upstream evaluation example, the consumer creates a Tcl interpreter, evaluates an in-memory sum-of-squares script, checks evaluation status and the integer result against Fortran, then destroys the interpreter. Tk graphical windows, extension modules, Tcl stubs and all bindings are not validated; the browser example requires no graphical display or network. Checked driver: Tcl computes sums of squares for n=0..64, compared with independent integer closed forms. One malformed expression must produce nonempty error text; a subsequent expression must return 56. One reused interpreter, no GUI/network. Other bindings, callbacks, arbitrary scripts and thread safety unverified.

Selected base_types, lib_algebra and lib_array modules, using the pinned revision immediately before the upstream FPM test suite introduced source symlinks. Nine checksum-guarded edits bring lib_array exactly to upstream commit 844611933cba06d71490033e68b355f6f0ff704f, retaining its integration-limit, descending histogram-bin and precision fixes. The other selected modules are unchanged. The ordinary archive policy remains unchanged. A synthetic FPM wrapper uses the already generated Fortran sources, not the Python templates. The checked consumer integrates the affine function 2*x+1 on [0,1], checks linear interpolation at an interior off-grid point, and solves x**2-5*x+6 against the exact roots 2 and 3. Additional checks cover integration limits outside the tabulated range, descending histogram bins and bin-center precision; the expanded example fails with the older unpatched array module and passes with the upstream fixes. GAMS F1 denotes the quadratic solver, not a general iterative root finder. Random sampling, statistics, geometry, HDF5/FITS bindings and other modules are not selected; the example does not validate every routine in the included modules. Dedicated F1 consumer verifies 84 real64 quadratic calls from 21 distinct dyadic root pairs and four signed coefficient scales, comparing sorted roots, root sums/products and normalized residuals. Uses only the ordinary quadratic API, not Pascal/reduced variants. Repeated/complex roots, zero leading coefficient, severe cancellation and extreme scaling are not verified. The separate E1 interpolation and H2 integration mappings remain source-supported.

Pinned Fiats tag 0.12.0 (upstream manifest version 0.11.1), named inference-engine at that revision, with an explicitly pinned compatible Julienne 1.3.1 dependency and Assert 1.7.0. Tag 0.14.0 was tried first but its consumer build cannot find Julienne modules because they are declared only as a development dependency. Single-image coarrays and long free-form lines are enabled. Based on the author's write-read-infer example, the checked consumer constructs a two-input ReLU network with known diagonal weights and biases, evaluates negative, zero and positive input pairs, and compares every output with direct formulas. K is a broad function-approximation classification; training algorithms, gradients, model-file round trips and parallel speedups are not verified. The historical version is explicit in the menu description. The original Berkeley Lab license terms, including the enhancements clause, are retained. The dedicated GAMS driver additionally checks 48 fixed multilayer networks with irregular widths, three activations, scalar references, padding sentinels and repeated inference; default identity input/output ranges only.

Standalone demonstration of the modern Julienne testing framework, with its pinned Assert dependency and single-image coarrays. The numerical source is unchanged. The checked consumer verifies an approximate real comparison and an exact integer sum, then deliberately creates a failed test_diagnosis_t, checks its failure flag and nonempty appended diagnostic and prints it while completing successfully. This demonstrates diagnosis construction and inspection rather than macro assertion termination. The full test harness, automatic test discovery, macro enforcement and multi-image behavior are not validated. Original Berkeley Lab/Sourcery Institute license terms and dependency notices are retained. Checked driver: 289 integer equality and 765 default-real absolute-tolerance outcomes, including exact boundary acceptance and zero tolerance. Inputs are exact dyadics and expected flags follow integer inequalities. One failed diagnosis retains an appended annotation. Relative/percentage tolerances, arrays, nonfinite inputs, macro termination and multi-image testing unverified.

Unmodified Fortran/C POSIX pipe interfaces in the restricted Linux sandbox. Following the upstream process_open_read example, the consumer opens a local printf command, reads and checks the integers 7 and 11, verifies end of output and requires a successful process_close status. Commands run under the ordinary sandbox restrictions; this does not add network or host-system access. Interactive terminals, graphical subprocesses, arbitrary process behavior, write pipes and Windows portability are not verified. Checked driver: Four fixed local printf read pipes return 170 independently generated integer records; order, end of output and successful process_close status are checked. Sandbox restrictions remain in effect. Write pipes, arbitrary commands, stderr/nonzero-status handling, interactive terminals and Windows behavior unverified.

Historical SciPy PROPACK 2.1 sources, whose repository is archived and explicitly points to rmlarsen/propack for the maintained implementation. The current author archive and tags v2.2/v2.1 exceed the unchanged source download limit, largely due to saved example outputs. The menu explicitly identifies this historical source choice. Only the native double-precision serial routines are wrapped, using the portable RISC modified Gram-Schmidt implementation and compatible system LP64 BLAS/LAPACK. Numerical sources are unchanged. A callback supplies multiplication by a rectangular diagonal matrix with known singular values. The consumer passes a writable convergence-count argument, requests the leading three singular triplets, and checks 12, 11 and 10, both A*v-sigma*u and transpose(A)*u-sigma*v residuals, finite values and unit vector norms. The restarted algorithm, other precisions, arbitrary sparse matrices and parallel performance are not verified.

Original one-dimensional nonuniform Fourier code using the dynamically allocated Fortran 90 interface and bundled Netlib FFT implementation. Forty-nine checksum-guarded edits change legacy extent-one FFT dummy-array declarations to assumed size; every changed array is checked against its containing procedure argument list. No local arrays, transform formulas or global bounds-checking settings are changed. Legacy workspace argument type punning is accepted with the package-specific -fallow-argument-mismatch option. The example evaluates a type-1 transform of 96 deterministic nonuniform points into 32 modes for both exponent signs and compares every complex coefficient with an independent direct sum, including the documented 1/nj normalization. Status and finite values are checked. Types 2/3, the static Fortran 77 interface and every bundled FFT routine are not verified. The class-specific J1 driver adds 24 type-1 transforms: 80 nonuniform sources, 15/16/31/32 modes, three deterministic strength patterns and both exponent signs, checked against independently accumulated trigonometric sums and the exact zero mode. Type 2/3 and performance remain unverified.

Original two-dimensional nonuniform Fourier code using the dynamically allocated Fortran 90 interface and bundled Netlib FFT implementation. Forty-nine checksum-guarded edits change legacy extent-one FFT dummy-array declarations to assumed size after checking that each is a procedure argument; no formulas or local arrays change and bounds checking remains enabled. Legacy workspace argument type punning uses the package-specific -fallow-argument-mismatch option. The example transforms 96 deterministic scattered points onto a 16-by-18 mode grid for both exponent signs, checking status, finite values and all coefficients against an independent direct sum with the documented 1/nj normalization. Types 2/3, the static Fortran 77 interface, every FFT routine and multidimensional performance are not verified.

Mixed C/Fortran source set selected from the upstream Waf library lists, wrapped for FPM with the bundled Lua 5.4.8 core and libraries, the C dump wrapper and GNU-supported extended/quad precision module variants. Lua command-line interpreter/compiler executables and upstream tests are excluded. Sources are unchanged; the operator-only wrapper now permits explicitly listed locked C files, retaining old adapter identities and the ordinary downloader/archive limits. The consumer creates a small Lua configuration, checks a computed integer, a double-precision scalar, two named nested-table entries and a missing-key default with error bits, closes the state and deletes its file. Broader scripting, dump/reload callbacks, every numeric kind and sandbox-restricted system operations are not verified. Checked driver: 32 fresh Lua configuration files with computed triangular integers, signed dyadic reals and nested table entries; five independent value/default references each, table lengths and missing-key status bits. Malformed scripts, wrong types, callbacks, dump/reload and general Lua operations unverified.

The unrelated qencode.c utility is excluded: its query parser refers to qstrtrim and qlisttbl routines absent from the archive. The library retains vector, list, set, hash-table and tree-table modules and their vendored C dependencies. The checked consumer exercises vector growth, indexing, replacement, array conversion, pop and clear, and string-keyed map insertion, replacement, lookup, missing-key lookup and clear. Block scope invokes finalizers. Integer payloads are used; general pointer ownership, all container methods and threading are not validated. Dedicated N4 driver: Independent plain-array/key-map oracle for eight C-backed integer traces: 51080 exact references for growth, index edits, FIFO pops, map updates and presence. Vector clear and map clear/reuse checked; vector append-after-clear resets C element size and has a retained failing probe. No library patch or successful vector-reuse claim. Object copying, iterators and thread safety unverified.

procedure_mappings.notes: Mixed C/Fortran operating-system utilities wrapped for FPM. Two checksum-guarded compatibility edits set the Linux os_name constant and restrict the ISO_C_BINDING import to avoid the Fortran 2023 F_C_STRING name collision. OS_SYSTEM_ID is configured as OS_LINUX. The checked consumer creates nested temporary directories and a 14-byte stream file, checks file size and type, basename/dirname and path normalization, then renames and deletes the file and removes both directories. No external files or user environment are required. This configured recipe and exported project target Linux; Windows branches, processes, user/home lookup and every path utility are not validated. Checked driver: 33 Linux file create/rename/read/unlink lifecycles with exact sizes and contents, relative/absolute normalization fixtures, basename/dirname, nested mkdir/rmdir. The upstream Fortran library source set is wrapped for FPM with pinned MPICH and OpenBLAS native dependencies. gFTL is a header/template library, not a standalone compiled library. Other templates/types, deletion, iterators, copies, clear/reuse and memory leaks unverified.

Eight 49-key mixed integer/REAL64/text/array dictionaries with exact reverse lookups, input-array mutation to check ownership, deletion survivors and explicit destruction. These direct solver checks do not extend the molecular verification scope.

A separate skew-cell probe returns 0.92970967292785645 where an independent periodic-image search gives 0.31679647220910667; source, hash and complete result are retained in docs/gams-candidates/raffle-skew. No library patch is made.

Original included parameter/interface sources and LGPL notices are retained. The sandbox must return a browser-viewable PNG, which is visually reviewed. Q covers graphics. Native C/Cairo libraries and fonts are installed only in this package image; no precompiled Debian Fortran module files are used by the consumer. Interactive windows, other output drivers and the full upstream example/test suite are not verified.

The unmodified M_history redo editor records two commands in its scratch history file. Checked driver: 12 generated original history commands, each recalled and edited with a scripted numeric substitution, then recalled again to require the unchanged original. Uses supported 1024-character line buffers and scratch directive units; no shell command is executed. Short buffers, other editing directives, interactive terminals and malformed history commands unverified.

The original M_CLI FPM library is unchanged. No stdin or program arguments are required; the editable prototype supplies the defaults. Actual command-line overrides, help/error paths and interactive examples are not runtime-verified here. N1/N3 cover command input and character parsing; no numerical-method classification is inferred. Public-domain/Unlicense notices are retained. Repeated calls exercise dictionary reinitialization. Actual CLI overrides, malformed input, help paths and all quoting rules unverified.
